   214	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   215	    exact (fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some u)
   216	
   217	/-- The rounded Fourier projectors resolve the identity on the enlarged space. -/
   218	theorem roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   219	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   220	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, roundedFourierPVM O hO u = 1 := by
   221	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : Fin t → ZMod 2))]
   222	  have hrest : ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, roundedFourierPVM O hO u =
   223	      ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u) := by
   224	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   225	    intro u hu
   226	    unfold roundedFourierPVM
   227	    rw [if_neg (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hu)]
   228	  rw [hrest]
   229	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   230	  rw [if_pos rfl, sub_add_cancel]

231	
   232	/-- Distinct rounded Fourier projectors are orthogonal.  This is the
   233	orthogonality of the projectors `C^u` invoked at
   234	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   235	theorem roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   236	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   237	    {u v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (huv : u ≠ v) :
   238	    roundedFourierPVM O hO u * roundedFourierPVM O hO v = 0 := by
   239	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   240	  by_cases hu : u = 0 <;> by_cases hv : v = 0
   241	  · exact absurd (hu.trans hv.symm) huv
   242	  · rw [if_pos hu, if_neg hv, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
   243	      sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv, sub_self]
   244	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_pos hv, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_one,
   245	      liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase O hO hu, sub_self]
   246	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_neg hv]
   247	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => huv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   248	
   249	/-- The rounded Fourier projective measurement `{C^u}`: the family
   250	`roundedFourierPVM` bundled as a POVM with outcomes in `F_2^t` acting on the
   251	enlarged space `ι × Option (F_2^t)`.  Positivity of each effect follows from
   252	`roundedFourierPVM_isProj` and completeness is `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`;
   253	the measurement is projective by `roundedFourierMeasurement_isProjective`, and
   254	distinct effects are orthogonal by `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`.  This
   255	is the projective measurement `{C^u}` produced by Naimark's theorem at
   256	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   257	def roundedFourierMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   258	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   259	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (Fin t → ZMod 2) (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   260	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   261	    (roundedFourierPVM O hO)
   262	    (fun u => (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).nonneg)
   263	    (roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one O hO)
   264	
   265	/-- The effects of the rounded Fourier measurement are the rounded Fourier
   266	projectors. -/
   267	@[simp]
   268	theorem roundedFourierMeasurement_effect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   269	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   270	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   271	    (roundedFourierMeasurement O hO).effect u = roundedFourierPVM O hO u :=
   272	  rfl
   273	
   274	/-- The rounded Fourier measurement is projective: every one of its effects is
   275	an orthogonal projection.  This is the projectivity of `{C^u}` invoked at
   276	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   277	theorem roundedFourierMeasurement_isProjective {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   278	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   279	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (roundedFourierMeasurement O hO) :=
   280	  fun u => roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u
   281	
   282	/-- The compression identity of the rounded Fourier projective measurement: for
   283	every operator `X` on the original space,
   284	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) C^u) = Tr(X B^u)`, where `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` is the
   285	Fourier-square effect.  For a nonzero outcome this is the expectation
   286	preservation of the one-measurement Naimark dilation; for the zero outcome it
   287	follows from the resolution of the identity by the `B^u`.  This is the sense in
   288	which `{C^u}` simulates `{B^u}` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   289	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   290	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   291	    (X : Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   292	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedFourierPVM O hO u) =
   293	      Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   294	  have hP : ∀ v : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   295	      Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) *
   296	          (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)) =
   297	        Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) := by
   298	    intro v
   299	    rw [ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   300	    unfold heteroKron
   301	    rw [trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect, fourierNaimarkData_source]
   302	    rfl
   303	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   304	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   305	  · rw [if_pos hu]
   306	    subst hu
   307	    have hone :
   308	        Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * 1) = Matrix.trace (X * 1) := by
   309	      rw [Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_one, ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   310	      unfold heteroKron naimarkAuxProjector
   311	      simpa using Matrix.trace_kronecker X
   312	        (Matrix.single (none : Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) none (1 : ℂ))
   313	    have hB : X * (operatorFourier O 0 * operatorFourier O 0) =
   314	        X * 1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) := by
   315	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Matrix.mul_sub]
   316	      congr 1
   317	      rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
   318	      exact (Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ
   319	        (fun v => operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) (Finset.mem_univ 0)).trans
   320	        (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   321	    rw [hB, Matrix.mul_sub, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sub, Matrix.trace_sub,
   322	      Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, hone]
   323	    congr 1
   324	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun v _ => hP v)
   325	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   326	    exact hP u
   327	
   328	/-! ## The rounded observables -/
   329	
   330	/-- The rounded observables `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u`, the signed sums of the
   331	rounded Fourier projectors.  These are the observables `𝒜(a)` introduced at
   332	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1100-1102`; the character `(-1)^{u·a}` is
   333	`booleanCharacter u a`. -/
   334	def roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   335	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   336	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   337	  ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • roundedFourierPVM O hO u
   338	
   339	/-- The exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}` of the rounded observables, for
   340	every pair of Boolean-group elements.  Expanding the product, the orthogonality
   341	and idempotence of the projectors `C^u` leave only the diagonal terms, and the
   342	characters multiply.  This is the deduction at
   343	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   344	theorem roundedObservable_mul {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   345	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   346	    (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   347	    roundedObservable O hO a * roundedObservable O hO b = roundedObservable O hO (a + b) := by
   348	  unfold roundedObservable
   349	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   350	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   351	  intro u _
   352	  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single u]
   353	  · rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul,
   354	      (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isIdempotentElem.eq, ← booleanCharacter_add_right]
   355	  · intro v _ hvu
   356	    rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne O hO hvu.symm,
   357	      smul_zero, smul_zero]
   358	  · intro hu
   359	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ u) hu
   360	
   361	/-- The rounded observable at the zero group element is the identity. -/
   362	theorem roundedObservable_zero {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   363	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   364	    roundedObservable O hO 0 = 1 := by
   365	  simp [roundedObservable, roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one]
   366	
   367	/-- The rounded observables are Hermitian: the characters are real and the
   368	rounded Fourier projectors are self-adjoint. -/
   369	theorem roundedObservable_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   370	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   371	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   372	    (roundedObservable O hO a).IsHermitian := by
   373	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, roundedObservable, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
   374	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   375	  intro u _
   376	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_booleanCharacter,
   377	    (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   378	
   379	/-- Every rounded observable is a binary observable: it is Hermitian, and its
   380	square is `L^{a+a} = L^0 = 1` by exact linearity. -/
   381	theorem roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   382	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   383	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   384	    IsBinaryObservable (roundedObservable O hO a) := by
   385	  refine ⟨roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO a, ?_⟩
   386	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
   387	    ext i
   388	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   389	  rw [roundedObservable_mul, haa, roundedObservable_zero]
   390	
   391	/-- The compression identity of the rounded observables: for every operator `X`
   392	on the original space,
   393	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) L^a) = Tr(X ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u)`.  The right-hand side
   394	is the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM whose overlap with `O^a` is
   395	certified by `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`; this is the passage
   396	from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to `Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
   397	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`. -/
   398	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   399	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   400	    (X : Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   401	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedObservable O hO a) =
   402	      Matrix.trace (X * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   403	        (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   404	  simp only [roundedObservable, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, mul_smul_comm,
   405	    Matrix.trace_smul, trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM]
   406	
   407	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Section 5 — Making measurements projective: definitions
     6	
     7	Definitions for Naimark dilation and orthonormalization, matching
     8	Section 5 of `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex` and
     9	Chapter 4 of the blueprint (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch04_projective.tex`).
    10	
    11	## Naimark dilation structure
    12	
    13	The key mathematical content is the **Naimark dilation theorem**: given
    14	submeasurements on a bipartite space, there exist auxiliary registers and
    15	projective measurements on the enlarged space that preserve all correlations
    16	exactly.
    17	
    18	### One-measurement Naimark (Lemma 5.2)
    19	
    20	The building block is the one-measurement Naimark lemma. Given a
    21	submeasurement `{M_a}_{a ∈ α}` on `Op d`, it produces a projective
    22	submeasurement on the enlarged space `Op (d × Option α)`. The auxiliary
    23	register has dimension `|α| + 1`, with the extra dimension absorbing the
    24	"missing mass" `I − ∑ M_a`. The construction uses the isometry
    25	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩` and defines
    26	`P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V`.
    27	
    28	### Questionwise Naimark data
    29	
    30	For a prospective full bipartite assembly, one-measurement Naimark is applied
    31	independently to each question on each side.  The current formal interface
    32	records these questionwise local data and their marginal preservation
    33	identities, not the full tensor-product correlation theorem.
    34	
    35	## Matrix-level witnesses
    36	
    37	Concrete `Matrix d d ℂ` witnesses are provided alongside the abstract
    38	operator-algebra formulation, giving honest probability and overlap formulas.
    39	-/

   174	
   175	/-! ### One-measurement Naimark dilation (Lemma 5.2)
   176	
   177	The one-measurement Naimark dilation is the building block for the full
   178	theorem. Given a submeasurement `M` on space `d`, it produces a projective
   179	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α`, where `Option α`
   180	models the auxiliary register with one extra dimension `none = ⊥` for the
   181	missing mass `I − ∑ M_a`. -/
   182	
   183	/-- The auxiliary pure-state projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` on `Option α`, where `⊥ = none`.
   184	This is the initial state of the auxiliary register before the Naimark
   185	isometry is applied. -/
   186	def naimarkAuxProjector (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   187	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   188	  Matrix.single none none 1
   189	
   190	/-- The lifted density matrix for one-measurement Naimark dilation:
   191	`ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)`.
   192	The scaling by `|Option α|` ensures the normalized trace is preserved:
   193	`τ'(ρ_lifted) = τ(ρ)`, where `τ'` is the normalized trace on the enlarged space. -/
   194	noncomputable def oneMeasLiftedDensity {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   195	    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   196	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   197	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   198	  (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • Matrix.kronecker ρ (naimarkAuxProjector α)
   199	
   200	/-- One-measurement Naimark dilation data at the matrix level.
   201	
   202	Given a submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, this witnesses the existence
   203	of a projective submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` that
   204	preserves all expectation values. This is Lemma 5.2 of the paper.
   205	
   206	The construction: let `V : H → H ⊗ ℂ^{|α|+1}` be the isometry
   207	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   208	Then `P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V` is a projection, and
   209	`⟨ψ|M_a|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ⊗⊥|P̂_a|ψ⊗⊥⟩`. -/
   210	structure OneMeasNaimarkData (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   211	    (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where

    18	/-- The Naimark column acts as an isometry on the input subspace: `VP = V`. -/
    19	private lemma oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj
    20	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    21	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    22	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :

    25	  ext ⟨d₁, oa₁⟩ ⟨d₂, oa₂⟩
    26	  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, oneMeasNaimarkInputProj,
    27	    oneMeasNaimarkAuxTransition]

    29	  | none =>

    31	        oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) x *
    32	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)

    54	-- This is independent of Naimark and could be moved to `LDT/Preliminaries`.
    55	/-- **Partial isometry to unitary extension** (general fact).
    56	
    57	If `V†V = P` where `P` is a projection and `V = VP`, then there exists
    58	a unitary `U` on the full space with `UP = V`.
    59	
    60	This is a standard result in finite-dimensional linear algebra: V is an
    61	isometry from range(P) to V's range, and in finite dimensions any
    62	isometry between subspaces extends to a unitary.
    63	
    64	**Mathlib route**: `LinearIsometry.extend` provides the extension for
    65	linear isometries between inner product spaces. The gap is the
    66	matrix-to-`EuclideanSpace` transport. -/
    67	private lemma partialIsometry_to_unitary
    68	    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    69	    (V P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)
    70	    (hP : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P)
    71	    (hVP : V * P = V)
    72	    (hVV : Vᴴ * V = P) :
    73	    ∃ U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ,
    74	      (U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P = V := by
    75	  classical
    76	  have toEuclideanLin_mul :
    77	      ∀ A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n,
    78	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) =
    79	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B) := by
    80	    intro A B
    81	    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same (p := (2 : ENNReal)) A B]
    82	  let Pₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin P
    83	  let Vₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin V
    84	  let S : Submodule ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := LinearMap.range Pₗ
    85	  letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ S := Submodule.innerProductSpace S
    86	  have hP_fix : ∀ x : S, Pₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = x := by
    87	    intro x
    88	    rcases x.2 with ⟨y, hy⟩
    89	    rw [← hy]
    90	    calc
    91	      Pₗ (Pₗ y) = (Pₗ.comp Pₗ) y := rfl
    92	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P * P) y := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    93	      _ = Pₗ y := by rw [hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
    94	  have hVP_lin : Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Vₗ := by
    95	    calc
    96	      Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (V * P) := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    97	      _ = Vₗ := by rw [hVP]
    98	  have hgram : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Pₗ := by
    99	    calc
   100	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Matrix.toEuclideanLin P := by rw [hVV]
   101	      _ = Pₗ := rfl
   102	  let Llin : S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Vₗ.comp S.subtype
   103	  have hLnorm : ∀ x : S, ‖Llin x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
   104	    exact (LinearMap.norm_map_iff_inner_map_map
   105	      (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := S) (E' := EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   106	      (F := S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n) Llin).2 fun x y => by
   107	      have hy : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = y := by
   108	        calc
   109	          Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) =
   110	              Pₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hgram]
   111	          _ = y := hP_fix y
   112	      calc
   113	        inner ℂ (Llin x) (Llin y) =
   114	            inner ℂ (Vₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) (Vₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := rfl
   115	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   116	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := by
   117	          dsimp [Vₗ]
   118	          rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   119	          exact (LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (𝕜 := ℂ)
   120	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   121	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n))).symm
   122	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hy]
   123	        _ = inner ℂ x y := rfl
   124	  let L : S →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := { toLinearMap := Llin, norm_map' := hLnorm }
   125	  let Ulin : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n :=
   126	    LinearIsometry.extend (𝕜 := ℂ) (V := EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (S := S) L
   127	  let Umat : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n :=
   128	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm Ulin.toLinearMap
   129	  have hUmat_lin : Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat = Ulin.toLinearMap := by
   130	    exact Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply Ulin.toLinearMap
   131	  have hUstarU : Umatᴴ * Umat = 1 := by
   132	    apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   133	    calc
   134	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Umatᴴ * Umat) =
   135	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat).adjoint.comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat) := by
   136	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   137	      _ = Ulin.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp Ulin.toLinearMap := by rw [hUmat_lin]
   138	      _ = 1 := by exact Ulin.adjoint_comp_self'
   139	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) := by
   140	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_one]
   141	            rfl
   142	  let U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ := ⟨Umat, (Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff').2 hUstarU⟩
   143	  refine ⟨U, ?_⟩
   144	  apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   145	  apply LinearMap.ext
   146	  intro x
   147	  have hExt : Ulin (Pₗ x) = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := by
   148	    simpa [Ulin, L, Llin] using
   149	      (LinearIsometry.extend_apply L ⟨Pₗ x, LinearMap.mem_range_self Pₗ x⟩)
   150	  calc
   151	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin ((U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P) x =
   152	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat (Pₗ x) := by
   153	          rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
   154	          rfl
   155	    _ = Ulin (Pₗ x) := by
   156	          rw [hUmat_lin]
   157	          rfl
   158	    _ = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := hExt
   159	    _ = Vₗ x := by
   160	          have hx := congrArg
   161	            (fun f : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n => f x) hVP_lin
   162	          simpa [LinearMap.comp_apply] using hx
   163	    _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin V x := rfl

   217	/-- **One-measurement Naimark lemma** (Lemma 5.2).
   218	
   219	For any submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, there exists a projective
   220	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` such that for every
   221	operator `ρ` on `Op d` and outcome `a`:
   222	`τ(ρ · M_a) = τ'(ρ_lifted · P̂_a)`
   223	where `ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)` and `P̂_a` is the
   224	dilated projector.
   225	
   226	**Proof sketch**: Let `V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   227	This is an isometry (by the submeasurement property `∑ M_a ≤ I`).
   228	Define `P̂_a = V†(I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|)V`. Then `P̂_a` is an orthogonal projection
   229	(since `|a⟩⟨a|` is), and the compression identity
   230	`(I⊗⟨⊥|) P̂_a (I⊗|⊥⟩) = √M_a · √M_a = M_a` gives the result.
   231	
   232	The proof uses `CFC.sqrt` for PSD operators together with lemmas such as
   233	`CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self`. -/
   234	theorem oneMeasNaimark {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   235	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   236	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :
   237	    OneMeasNaimarkLemma α d M := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let auxProj : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   240	    fun oa => Matrix.single oa oa 1
   241	  /-
   242	  The prescribed Naimark isometry column:
   243	    `V (|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩)
   244	      = ∑_a √(M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I - ∑_a M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`,
   245	  encoded by `oneMeasNaimarkColumn M`.  Concretely, this matrix is
   246	  supported only on the input `none = ⊥` slice.
   247	  -/
   248	  let V : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) := oneMeasNaimarkColumn M
   249	  /-
   250	  Extend the isometry column `V` to a unitary `U` on the whole enlarged space.
   251	  The dilated projectors are then `U† (I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|) U`.
   252	  -/
   253	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
   254	    partialIsometry_to_unitary
   255	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn M) (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d))
   256	      oneMeasNaimarkInputProj_isProj
   257	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj M)
   258	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn_isometry M)
   259	  let Umat : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) := U
   260	  refine ⟨{
   261	    source := M
   262	    liftedEffect := fun oa =>
   263	      Umatᴴ * Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) * Umat
   264	    lifted_isProj := ?_
   265	    lifted_sum_le_one := ?_
   266	    expectation_preservation := ?_
   267	  }, rfl⟩
   268	  · intro oa
   269	    /-
   270	    `U† (I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|) U` is a projection because `I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|` is, and
   271	    conjugation by a unitary preserves Hermitian idempotents.
   272	    -/
   273	    let P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   274	      Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa)
   275	    have hPproj : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P := by
   276	      exact isProj_kronecker
   277	        ((IsStarProjection.one _))
   278	        (optionBasisProj_isProj oa)
   279	    simpa [Umat, P] using isProj_unitary_conj U hPproj
   280	  · /-
   281	    Since the auxiliary rank-one projectors sum to the identity on `Option α`,
   282	    the lifted family is actually a complete projective measurement, hence in
   283	    particular a submeasurement.
   284	    -/
   285	    have hauxDecomp : ∑ oa : Option α, auxProj oa = auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a) := by
   286	      exact Fintype.sum_option (f := auxProj)
   287	    have hsplit :
   288	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) =
   289	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj none) +
   290	            ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) := by
   291	      exact Fintype.sum_option
   292	          (f := fun oa : Option α =>
   293	            Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa))
   294	    have hsumSome :
   295	        ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) =
   296	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (∑ a : α, auxProj (some a)) := by
   297	      ext x y
   298	      rcases x with ⟨i, oi⟩
   299	      rcases y with ⟨j, oj⟩
   300	      by_cases hij : i = j
   301	      · subst hij
   302	        rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
   303	        simp [Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply]
   304	      · rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
   305	        simp [Matrix.kronecker, hij]
   306	    have hauxSplit : auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a) = 1 := by
   307	      rw [← hauxDecomp, optionBasisProj_sum_eq_one]
   308	    have hbase :
   309	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) = 1 := by
   310	      calc
   311	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa)
   312	            = Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj none) +
   313	                ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) := by
   314	                  exact hsplit

   316	              (auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a)) := by
   317	                rw [hsumSome]
   318	                simpa using
   319	                  (Matrix.kronecker_add

   372	    (roundedObservable O hO a).IsHermitian := by
   373	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, roundedObservable, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
   374	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   375	  intro u _
   376	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_booleanCharacter,
   377	    (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   378	
   379	/-- Every rounded observable is a binary observable: it is Hermitian, and its
   380	square is `L^{a+a} = L^0 = 1` by exact linearity. -/
   381	theorem roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   382	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   383	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   384	    IsBinaryObservable (roundedObservable O hO a) := by
   385	  refine ⟨roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO a, ?_⟩
   386	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
   387	    ext i
   388	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   389	  rw [roundedObservable_mul, haa, roundedObservable_zero]
   390	
   391	/-- The compression identity of the rounded observables: for every operator `X`
   392	on the original space,
   393	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) L^a) = Tr(X ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u)`.  The right-hand side
   394	is the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM whose overlap with `O^a` is
   395	certified by `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`; this is the passage
   396	from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to `Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
   397	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`. -/
   398	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   399	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   400	    (X : Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   401	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedObservable O hO a) =
   402	      Matrix.trace (X * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   403	        (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   404	  simp only [roundedObservable, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, mul_smul_comm,
   405	    Matrix.trace_smul, trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM]
   406	
   407	end

     3	/-!
     4	# The quantum linearity theorem
     5	
     6	This file proves the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick in the
     7	form used to combine the binary observables produced in the point analysis.
     8	A family of binary observables indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`, whose
     9	two-query linearity correlation weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ` is at least `1 - δ`, is close on average, in the state-dependent
    11	distance weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, to an exactly linear family of binary
    12	observables on a finite ancillary extension.
    13	
    14	The proof assembles two results of the linearity route: the operator BLR bound
    15	`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, which converts the correlation
    16	hypothesis into the bound `2δ` on the average multiplicative defect
    17	`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2`, and Boolean representation stability
    18	`exists_exact_boolean_representation`, which converts that defect bound into
    19	the exactly linear family with the same average distance bound.  The notions
    20	in which the theorem is stated are in
    21	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.
    22	
    23	## Main results
    24	
    25	* `exists_exactly_linear_observables`: the theorem, with the closeness measured
    26	  by the squared state-dependent operator distance `stateDepDistSq` and the
    27	  bound `2 * δ`.
    28	* `exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`: the same
    29	  conclusion measured by the binary-measurement distance
    30	  `binaryObservableDistSq`, with the bound `δ` intended by the source.
    31	
    32	## References
    33	
    34	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-231`.  The QPBT paper quotes
    36	the theorem at
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    38	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
    39	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`.  The normalization of the
    40	distance bound is analyzed in
    41	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
    42	-/

    52	
    53	/-- The quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan--Vidick.  Let `t` be positive,
    54	`δ ≥ 0`, `ρ` a positive semidefinite trace-one operator on a finite carrier,
    55	and `O^u`, for `u ∈ F_2^t`, binary observables whose two-query correlation
    56	satisfies `E_{u,u'} Re Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ) ≥ 1 - δ`.  Then there are a
    57	finite ancillary carrier, a unit vector `anc` in it, and binary observables
    58	`L^u` on the product carrier such that `L^u L^{u'} = L^{u+u'}` for all `u, u'`
    59	and `E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 ≤ 2δ`, where `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`.
    60	
    61	This is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick,
    62	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`, hypothesis as in its display
    63	(7) and conclusion as in its display (8), stated as `thm:linearity` in
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`; the QPBT paper quotes
    65	it at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    66	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 233--280), this form
    67	imposes no upper bound on `δ`, asserts exact linearity for every pair, and
    68	averages closeness only over `u`.  The quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases
    69	closeness pointwise under a pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three
    70	deviations are not reproduced.  The identity at zero follows from exact
    71	linearity and the binary-observable condition.
    72	
    73	**Local fix:** The source prints the closeness bound as `δ` for the squared
    74	state-dependent operator distance.  Its calculation at
    75	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912` bounds the squared distance between
    76	the binary projective measurements of the observables, which is half the
    77	squared operator distance, and then identifies the two quantities; the operator
    78	bound `δ` is refuted by a four-point counterexample, and the bound established
    79	by the Fourier--Naimark argument is `2 * δ` for `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently
    80	`δ` for `binaryObservableDistSq`
    81	(`exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq`).  Documented in
    82	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex` and
    83	`rem:linearity-distance-normalization` (blueprint lines 282--301).
    84	
    85	The proof passes the correlation hypothesis through the operator BLR bound
    86	`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, obtaining
    87	`E_{u,u'} d_ρ(O^u O^{u'}, O^{u+u'})^2 ≤ 2δ`, and applies Boolean representation
    88	stability `exists_exact_boolean_representation` with `η = 2δ`. -/
    89	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    90	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    91	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    92	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    93	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    94	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    95	    (hcorrelation :
    96	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    97	        (uniformDistribution
    98	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    99	        (fun pair =>
   100	          (Matrix.trace
   101	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
   102	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
   103	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
   104	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
   105	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
   106	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
   107	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
   108	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   109	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
   110	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   111	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ 2 * δ :=
   112	  exists_exact_boolean_representation t ht (2 * δ) (by linarith) ρ hρ htrace O hO
   113	    (avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error O hO ρ hρ htrace δ hcorrelation)
   114	
   115	/-- The quantum linearity theorem with the closeness measured by the distance
   116	between the binary projective measurements associated with the observables:
   117	under the hypotheses of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the exactly linear
   118	family satisfies `E_u d^{bin}_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 ≤ δ`.  This is the bound of
   119	display (8) of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick,
   120	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1083-1086`, in the measurement-distance
   121	convention of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:876-900`, the convention in
   122	which the source's calculation is correct; see
   123	`rem:linearity-distance-normalization`
   124	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:282-301`) and
   125	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.  It follows from
   126	`exists_exactly_linear_observables` by halving, through
   127	`binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two`. -/
   128	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type}
   129	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   130	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
   131	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   132	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   133	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
   134	    (hcorrelation :
   135	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
   136	        (uniformDistribution
   137	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   138	        (fun pair =>
   139	          (Matrix.trace
   140	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
   141	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
   142	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
   143	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
   144	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
   145	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
   146	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
   147	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   148	              (fun u => binaryObservableDistSq (L u)
   149	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   150	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ δ := by
   151	  obtain ⟨ι', hF, hD, anc, hanc, L, hL, hlin, hdist⟩ :=
   152	    exists_exactly_linear_observables t ht δ hδ ρ hρ htrace O hO hcorrelation
   153	  refine ⟨ι', hF, hD, anc, hanc, L, hL, hlin, ?_⟩
   154	  calc
   155	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   156	        (fun u => binaryObservableDistSq (L u) (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   157	          (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) =
   158	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   159	          (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u) (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   160	            (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc)) / 2) :=
   161	      avgOver_congr _ _ _
   162	        (fun u => binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two _ _ _)
   163	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   164	          (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u) (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   165	            (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) / 2 := by
   166	      simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
   167	      exact avgOver_mul_const _ _ _
   168	    _ ≤ 2 * δ / 2 := by gcongr
   169	    _ = δ := by ring
   170	
   171	end

     3	/-!
     4	# Boolean representation stability
     5	
     6	This file completes the proof of the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan
     7	and Vidick in its multiplicative-defect formulation.  A family of
     8	binary observables `O^u`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t` and weighted by a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator `ρ`, whose products `O^u O^v` are on
    10	average close to `O^{u+v}` in the state-dependent distance, is on average close,
    11	in the same distance and weighted by the extended state `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, to
    12	an exactly linear family of binary observables on an ancillary extension.
    13	
    14	The extension, the ancillary vector, and the exactly linear family are those
    15	of the Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM.  The main computation is
    16	an identity, not an inequality: the average squared state-dependent operator
    17	distance between the rounded family and the ampliated original family,
    18	weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, equals the average multiplicative defect of the
    19	original family weighted by `ρ`.  Both sides equal
    20	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The left side reduces to the
    21	correlation by compressing the rounded observables along the ancillary vector
    22	and applying the cubic Fourier identity; the right side is the operator BLR
    23	computation, including the reindexing of the uniform pair.  No commutation
    24	among the observables is assumed, and the weight `ρ` is never replaced by the
    25	normalized trace.
    26	
    27	## Main results
    28	
    29	* `heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef` and `trace_heteroKron_ancProj`: the extended
    30	  weight `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` is again positive semidefinite with trace one.
    31	* `re_trace_roundedObservable_mul_heteroKron`: the compression of the
    32	  correlation between a rounded observable and the ampliated original
    33	  observable to the original space.
    34	* `stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable`: the pointwise distance between a rounded
    35	  observable and the ampliated original observable, in terms of the overlap
    36	  with the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM.
    37	* `avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect`: the
    38	  distance/defect identity
    39	  `E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 = E_{u,v} d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2`.
    40	* `exists_exact_boolean_representation`: the Boolean representation stability
    41	  theorem, obtained by weakening the identity to the incoming bound.
    42	
    43	## References
    44	
    45	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 and its Fourier/Naimark
    46	proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the closing step, which
    47	converts the overlap certificate into the distance bound, is at lines
    48	1104--1112, and the state-dependent distance is defined at lines 866--900.
    49	The QPBT paper quotes the theorem at
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.  The
    51	blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    52	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-147`, and the
    53	correlation-form statement is `exists_exactly_linear_observables` in
    54	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean`.  The declarations of this file are
    55	collected in the blueprint as `lem:boolean-representation-stability`.  The
    56	normalization convention, under which the incoming average multiplicative
    57	defect and the outgoing average squared state-dependent operator distance
    58	carry the same constant, is recorded in
    59	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
    60	-/
    61	
    62	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    63	
    64	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    65	
    66	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    67	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    68	
    69	noncomputable section
    70	
    71	/-! ## The extended weight -/
    72	
    73	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the extended state
    74	`ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1081-1082`: the
    75	rank-one density of any vector is positive semidefinite. -/
    76	theorem ancProj_posSemidef {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    77	    (ancProj v).PosSemidef :=
    78	  Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star _
    79	
    80	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the extended state
    81	`ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1081-1082`: the
    82	trace of the rank-one density of a vector is the square of its norm. -/
    83	theorem trace_ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    84	    Matrix.trace (ancProj v) = (‖v‖ : ℂ) ^ 2 := by
    85	  have h := inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K (𝕜 := ℂ) v
    86	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct] at h
    87	  exact (Matrix.trace_vecMulVec _ _).trans h
    88	
    89	/-- The extended weight `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` of a positive semidefinite operator
    90	`ρ` and an ancillary vector is positive semidefinite.  Together with
    91	`trace_heteroKron_ancProj` this is the assertion that `ρ'` is a density
    92	operator on the extended space at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1081-1082`. -/
    93	theorem heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    94	    {ρ : Op ι} (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') :
    95	    (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc)).PosSemidef :=
    96	  hρ.kronecker (ancProj_posSemidef anc)
    97	
    98	/-- The extended weight `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` of a trace-one operator `ρ` and a unit
    99	vector `anc` has trace one.  Together with `heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef` this
   100	is the assertion that `ρ'` is a density operator on the extended space at
   101	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1081-1082`. -/
   102	theorem trace_heteroKron_ancProj {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
   103	    (ρ : Op ι) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   104	    (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (hanc : ‖anc‖ = 1) :
   105	    (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc)).trace = 1 := by
   106	  unfold heteroKron
   107	  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
   108	  rw [Matrix.trace_kronecker, htrace, trace_ancProj, hanc]
   109	  simp
   110	
   111	/-- The ampliation `O ⊗ 1` of a binary observable by the identity of an
   112	ancillary space is a binary observable.  This is the sense in which the
   113	original observables `A(a)` act on the extended space in display (8) of

   115	theorem isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   116	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] {O : Op ι} (hO : IsBinaryObservable O) :
   117	    IsBinaryObservable (heteroKron O (1 : Op ι')) := by
   118	  unfold heteroKron
   119	  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
   120	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   121	  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hO.1.eq, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   122	  · rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, hO.2, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.one_kronecker_one]

   124	/-! ## The distance/defect identity -/
   125	
   126	/-- The correlation between a rounded observable `L^u` and the ampliated
   127	original observable `O^u ⊗ 1`, evaluated in the extended state
   128	`ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, has the same real part as the overlap between `O^u` and the

   131	Hermitian factors, after which the ampliated observable is absorbed into the
   132	weight and the rounded observable is compressed along the ancillary vector.
   133	This is the passage from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to
   134	`Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
   135	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`, with the operator order of the
   136	Lean distance preserved. -/

   138	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   139	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   140	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   141	    (Matrix.trace (roundedObservable O hO u *
   142	        heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   143	        heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))).re =
   144	      (Matrix.trace (O u * (∑ v : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter v u •
   145	        (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) * ρ)).re := by
   146	  have hL := roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO u
   147	  have hT := (isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one (ι' := Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) (hO u)).1

   149	    (heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef hρ _).isHermitian
   150	  have hprod : heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) *
   151	      heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) =
   152	        heteroKron (ρ * O u) (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) := by
   153	    unfold heteroKron

   155	    rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
   156	  have hstar :

   160	        Matrix.trace (O u * (∑ v : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter v u •
   161	          (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) * ρ) := by
   162	    calc
   163	      star (Matrix.trace (roundedObservable O hO u *
   164	          heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   165	          heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))) =

   168	            heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))ᴴ) := by

   171	            (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *

   173	        simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hL.eq, hT.eq, hρ'.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]

   194	theorem stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
   195	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   196	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))

    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.

    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary

   108	
   109	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   110	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   111	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   112	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   113	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   114	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   115	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   116	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   117	implementation.

   119	\section{When to Write a Note}
   120	
   121	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   122	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   123	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   124	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   125	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   126	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   127	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   128	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   129	relation.
   130	
   131	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   132	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   133	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   134	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   135	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   136	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   137	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   138	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   139	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   140	
   141	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   142	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   143	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   144	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   145	
   146	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   147	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   148	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   149	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   150	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   151	though it were the paper theorem.
   152	
   153	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   154	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   155	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   156	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   157	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   158	argument.
   159	
   160	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   161	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   162	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   163	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   164	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   165	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   166	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   167	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   168	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   169	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   170	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   171	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   172	
   173	\section{Counterexamples}
   174	
   175	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   176	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   177	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   178	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   179	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   180	
   181	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   182	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   183	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   184	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   185	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   186	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   187	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   188	
   189	\section{Revision of a Note}
   190

191	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   192	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   193	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   194	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   195	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   196	which point remains unsettled.
   197	
   198	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   199	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   200	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   201	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   202	discussion.
   203	
   204	\section{Form of the Note}
   205	
   206	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
   207	source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
   208	original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
   209	be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
   210	recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
   211	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
   212	around the mathematical assertion and its proof.
   213	
   214	The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
   215	measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
   216	should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
   217	state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
   218	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   219	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   220	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.
   221	
   222	Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
   223	substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
   224	a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
   225	proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
   226	logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.
   227	
   228	Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
   229	source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
   230	the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
   231	displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
   232	the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
   233	assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
   234	right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
   235	if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
   236	display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
   237	forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
   238	scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
   239	sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
   240	formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.
   241	
   242	Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
   243	\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
   244	\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
   245	the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
   246	equations.
   247	
   248	Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
   249	\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
   250	\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
   251	whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
   252	and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.
   253	
   254	The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
   255	there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
   256	in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
   257	be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
   258	footnotes.
   259	
   260	The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,
   261	that the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a
   262	harmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level
   263	gap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the
   264	mathematics, not the amount of formal work required.
   265	
   266	\section{Decision Principle}
   267	
   268	The formal development should not silently replace the cited assertion by a
   269	different one.  If the formal statement differs from the cited source, the
   270	reason for the difference should be written down.  Conversely, the note should
   271	not overstate the conclusion.  A wrong intermediate scalar is not a fatal gap in
   272	the theorem if the corrected scalar is bounded by the error parameter appearing
   273	in the theorem statement.
   274	
   275	\end{document}

@@ -0,0 +1,249 @@
+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+
+\newcommand{\dbin}{d^{\mathrm{bin}}}
+\newcommand{\Id}{\mathrm{Id}}
+\providecommand{\gapnote}[2]{\par\noindent\textbf{Verdict:} #1 (#2).\par}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+
+\title{Distance Normalization in the Quantum Linearity Theorem}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-04}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+\gapnote{false-source}{resolved}
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The factor-of-two calculation is
+  elementary, but the counterexample must remain valid after the ancillary
+  extension allowed by the theorem.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal adapter consists of one binary
+  effect definition and two distance identities, requiring roughly 70--100
+  lines of matrix algebra.  The source-facing theorem is stated with the
+  corrected bound.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} About 60\% is direct finite-matrix and
+  finite-sum algebra; the remaining 40\% is the project-local Boolean Fourier
+  and state-dependent distance interface.
+  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs.} Finite sums on the Boolean cube, complex
+  matrices and conjugate transpose, cyclicity of trace, and simultaneous
+  spectral decomposition for commuting Hermitian matrices.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $S$ and $T$ be binary observables and let $\rho$ be a positive
+semidefinite operator of trace one.  We distinguish the state-dependent
+operator distance from the distance between their associated binary projective
+measurements:
+\begin{align*}
+  d_\rho(S,T)^2
+    &:= \Re\tr\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big), \\
+  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
+    &:= \sum_{s\in\{+,-\}}
+      \Re\tr\big((P_S^s-P_T^s)^\dagger
+                       (P_S^s-P_T^s)\rho\big),
+  \qquad P_S^\pm := \frac{\Id\pm S}{2}.
+\end{align*}
+The normalization and correlation identities are
+\begin{align}
+  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2 &= \frac12 d_\rho(S,T)^2,
+    \tag{normalization}\label{eq:normalization}\\
+  d_\rho(S,T)^2
+    &= 2-2\Re\tr(ST\rho),
+    \tag{operator correlation}\label{eq:operator-correlation}\\
+  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
+    &= 1-\Re\tr(ST\rho).
+    \tag{binary correlation}\label{eq:binary-correlation}
+\end{align}
+Consequently, the conclusion delivered by the quantum linearity argument can
+be written either as
+\[
+  \mathbb E_a\dbin_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq\delta
+\]
+or, equivalently, as
+\[
+  \mathbb E_a d_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq2\delta.
+\]
+These are not equivalent to the same bound $\delta$ for the mean squared
+state-dependent operator distance.%
+\footnote{The formal declarations are \leanid{binaryObservableEffect},
+\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq},
+\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_stateDepDistSq\_div\_two},
+\leanid{stateDepDistSq\_eq\_two\_sub\_two\_mul\_correlation}, and
+\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_one\_sub\_correlation} in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean}.}
+
+\section{The source calculation}
+
+Natarajan and Vidick define the distance between two POVMs by summing the
+squared state-dependent distances between corresponding square roots
+\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  For projective measurements the
+square roots are the effects themselves.  In the binary case their calculation
+expands $P_S^\pm=(\Id\pm S)/2$ and obtains
+\[
+  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
+    = 1-\frac12\tr_\rho(ST+TS)
+    = \frac12\tr_\rho((S-T)^2).
+  \tag{source equation (3)}
+\]
+This is equation~(3) at lines~903--910 of the in-repository source mirror.%
+\footnote{See
+\path{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex}, lines~866--912.  The quantum
+linearity theorem and its Fourier--Naimark proof are at lines~1074--1112.}
+The next line identifies the final expression with the squared state-dependent
+operator distance.  The operator-distance definition at lines~873--875 is
+printed with $\rho$ occurring twice,
+\[
+  d_\rho(S,T)^2 = \tr_\rho\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big),
+  \qquad \tr_\rho(X) := \tr(\rho X),
+\]
+and we read the duplication as typographical, keeping the single $\rho$ of the
+definition of $d$ above.  Under that reading the squared state-dependent
+operator distance is $\tr_\rho((S-T)^2)$ rather than one half of that
+quantity.  Thus the calculation through line~910 is correct and the equality
+on line~911 loses a factor of two.
+
+The Fourier--Naimark proof is consistent with the measurement normalization.
+It proves
+\[
+  \mathbb E_a\operatorname{CON}_{\rho'}(A(a),\mathcal A(a))
+  = \frac12+\frac12\mathbb E_{a,b}
+       \tr_\rho(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)).
+\]
+The hypothesis therefore makes the consistency deficit at most $\delta/2$.
+For binary projective measurements, the squared measurement distance is twice
+that deficit, giving the bound $\delta$ for the squared binary-measurement
+distance and the bound $2\delta$ for the squared state-dependent operator
+distance.
+
+\section{A four-point counterexample}
+
+The bound $\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator distance is
+false.  Let $G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2$, choose $r\in G\setminus\{0\}$, take
+the one-dimensional state $\rho=1$, and define scalar binary observables by
+\[
+  A(a)=\begin{cases}
+    -1,&a=r,\\
+     1,&a\neq r.
+  \end{cases}
+\]
+For the characters $\chi_u(a)=(-1)^{u\cdot a}$, the normalized Fourier
+coefficients satisfy
+\[
+  \widehat A(0)=\frac12,
+  \qquad
+  \widehat A(u)=-\frac12\chi_u(r)\quad(u\neq0).
+\]
+Their multiset is
+$\{\frac12,\frac12,\frac12,-\frac12\}$, and hence
+\[
+  \mathbb E_{a,b}A(a)A(b)A(a+b)
+    =\sum_u\widehat A(u)^3=\frac14.
+\]
+The correlation hypothesis therefore holds with $\delta=3/4$.
+
+Every scalar exact Boolean representation is one of the characters $\chi_u$,
+and its mean squared state-dependent operator distance from $A$ is
+\[
+  \mathbb E_a |A(a)-\chi_u(a)|^2
+    =2-2\widehat A(u)\geq1.
+\]
+Allowing an ancillary space does not reduce this lower bound.  Exact linearity
+and the binary-observable relations make the operators $\mathcal A(a)$ a
+commuting family of Hermitian involutions.  Their simultaneous spectral
+subspaces carry characters of $G$.  Evaluation in any density operator is
+therefore a convex combination of the scalar character correlations above, so
+the mean squared state-dependent operator distance remains at least $1$.  It
+cannot be at most $\delta=3/4$.  By~\eqref{eq:normalization}, the corresponding
+mean squared binary-measurement distance has lower bound $1/2$, which is
+compatible with the provider's conclusion.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+
+The QPBT paper quotes the quantum linearity theorem at lines~711--725 of its
+Pauli-basis analysis and defers its proof to Natarajan and Vidick.%
+\footnote{See
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
+lines~711--725.}
+The active blueprint expands the conclusion's distance as the state-dependent
+operator distance $d$ and states the bound $2\delta$, together with the
+equivalent bound $\delta$ for $\dbin$.  The formal theorem
+\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} bounds the average over $u$
+of \leanid{stateDepDistSq} by $2\delta$, and its companion
+\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables\_binaryObservableDistSq}
+bounds the average of \leanid{binaryObservableDistSq} by $\delta$; the
+printed bound $\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator
+distance is not reproduced.%
+\footnote{See
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~104--150, and
+the two declarations in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean}.}
+
+The mathematical content of the theorem is nevertheless available in the
+correct normalization.  The stability theorem
+\leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} assumes the mean squared
+state-dependent multiplicative defect
+\[
+  \mathbb E_{a,b}\, d_\rho\big(A(a)A(b), A(a+b)\big)^2 \le \eta
+\]
+and produces an ancillary space, a unit vector $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ in it and
+an exactly linear family $\{\mathcal A(a)\}$ of binary observables with
+$\mathbb E_a\, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a), A(a)\otimes\Id)^2 \le \eta$, where
+$\rho' = \rho \otimes \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$.
+Its bound rests on an identity rather than an inequality:
+\leanid{avg\_stateDepDistSq\_roundedObservable\_eq\_avg\_multiplicativeDefect}
+proves that the two averages above coincide, both being $2-2C$ for the
+two-query correlation
+$C = \mathbb E_{a,b}\Re\tr(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)\rho)$ of the linearity test.%
+\footnote{Both declarations are in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Stability.lean}; the blueprint
+records them as \texttt{lem:boolean-representation-stability}.}
+The source hypothesis $C \ge 1-\delta$ is therefore exactly the hypothesis of
+the stability theorem with $\eta = 2\delta$, and the theorem then yields the
+mean squared state-dependent operator distance bound $2\delta$: the corrected
+conclusion identified above, with no restriction on $\delta$ and no commutation
+assumption on the $A(a)$.  This reparameterization is the entire
+content of the repair, and the corrected source-facing statement
+\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} is obtained from
+\leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} by substituting
+$\eta = 2\delta$.
+
+The Boolean Fourier foundation keeps the state-dependent operator distance
+unchanged and adds the separately named binary-measurement distance together
+with equations~\eqref{eq:normalization}--\eqref{eq:binary-correlation}.  The
+statement repair changed the conclusion to mean squared state-dependent
+operator distance at most $2\delta$, added the equivalent form with mean
+squared binary-measurement distance at most $\delta$, and synchronized the
+blueprint; the realigned theorem is proved by the Fourier--Naimark argument,
+with the distance/defect relation established as an equality, that is, by the
+stability theorem under the reparameterization just described.%
+\footnote{The normalization investigation was tracked in
+\ghissue{124}; the source-facing statement repair was carried out in
+\ghissue{129}.}
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor
+$1/2$ in equation~(3), but its final identification with the squared
+state-dependent operator distance is incorrect.  The theorem proved by the
+Fourier--Naimark argument has mean squared binary-measurement error at most
+$\delta$, equivalently mean squared state-dependent operator error at most
+$2\delta$.  The four-point example rules out the printed bound $\delta$ for
+the mean squared state-dependent operator distance even when arbitrary
+ancillary extensions are allowed.  The blueprint theorem and the formal
+declarations carry the corrected bounds.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}
